I'm hoping someone can direct me on this. The back-story:

* Running Mint 17.3. * Want to give a HDD to a friend with Mint pre-installed. * Booted off Linux Mint LIVE USB stick * Plugged in external HDD to install Mint on * Did "Something else" for partitions, and created /, /boot, /home and swap on the external HDD * Set the external HDD to be the boot device (I assume for MBR to be written to it) * I have UEFI enabled in my BIOS

The install went great. However, now when I reboot, my machine will *only* boot to this external drive. It "lost" the settings for booting off my internal drive. Here is a potential rub: My internal drive is full-disk encrypted with LUKS/dm-crypt.

Is this just a matter of reconfiguring GRUB?

#Update I have fixed it! The solution was much simpler than I thought. The steps:

* Boot off external HDD * Mount the encrypted drives * Re-run update-grub (which then finds the install on the decrypted drives)

Rebooting allows me to select to boot on the encrypted drives. I enter my key, and voila! I am back in.

The way reddit chooses to comply with COPPA is by limiting account registration to those 13 and over. See this privacy policy section. That way they avoid the headaches of having to deal with regulations which are costly to comply with. If they do find out you're under 13, the safest and easiest way for them to comply with COPPA is to delete your account and all info associated with it.
